findings.reason: the node would either fail its gate or write outside its scope, and the fix is to add `reckon/_store.py` to the write paths and name the comment-append caller, or to drop case 2.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — verified all cited code anchors: reckon/evidence.py:407 (the count sentence), reckon/evidence.py:636 (synthesize_landed_record, refusal of a plan with no ledger rows at 662), reckon/_store.py:1184 and 1194 (_landed_record_shell delegates to _render_document with []), reckon/_store.py:1263 (append_evidence creating the shell), reckon/_store.py:993 (_prose_deferred_work_term), reckon/doccheck.py:412 and 419 (DEFERRED_WORK_TERM_IN_PROSE, the follow-ons regex); reckon audit-doc resolves to project_maintenance_commands.py:1618; the cross-repo anchors resolve too — power_convertor commit f7f7d2d6d exists and docs/evidence/archive/filter-recommendation-for-coil-health-landed.html carries the quoted "0 committed run(s)" sentence verbatim.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's first case asserts "text contains no 'committed run(s)' sentence", but the shell emits that sentence in two places and only one of them is document text.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2 puts every log under the run directory starting with its revision and literal command and ending EXIT=, and §3 records the audit command's output and finding count there; both are durable, neither is a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the two new test filenames name the mechanism (test_an_appended_record_claims_no_counts, test_every_spelling_of_deferred_work_is_read) and no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag appears in any proposed symbol, file or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §3 widens one regex, but no production caller refuses a comment body, so the mechanism does not run on the path its own done-when measures.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 is one deliverable (the append-created shell stops claiming counts) and §3 is one (the deferred-work term reads every spelling); the widening in §3 is one regex with a shared reader, not two goals.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — plan-after="a-finished-plan-closes" resolves to docs/plans/a-finished-plan-closes.html and satisfies the schema's wiring minimum for a plan in implementable state; §2 and §3 write disjoint files (reckon/_store.py + reckon/evidence.py vs reckon/doccheck.py) and declare no section-level wait, so no depends-on/informs/gates relationship is missing.
